title: subtoken-normalizer-hybrid-constraint-streaming-toolcall-safety
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Improves streaming stability for structured output by normalizing tokenizer subtokens and safely composing regex+CFG constraint backends; reduces tokenization-induced false constraint violations and decreases dropped-stream incidents.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a subtoken normalization shim and a lightweight hybrid constraint dispatcher to improve structured-output constrained decoding in streaming scenarios (particularly for tool/function-calling payloads).
Motivation: several customers reported spurious constraint failures and truncated toolcall frames when clients streamed partial tokens or when the tokenizer produced different subtoken boundaries across model variants (ENG-4521).
Root causes: 1) regex/CFG backends assumed token/byte boundaries that didn't hold during streaming; 2) partial subtokens could satisfy or violate anchors unpredictably; 3) streaming backpressure and early flush introduced partial-match windows that caused dropped toolcall delimiters.
Changes (high level):
- Add Subtoken Normalizer: a deterministic mapping layer that converts tokenizer subtokens into a canonical normalized sequence used by constraint backends. The normalizer performs grapheme-aware merging for common split cases (punctuation, quotes, Unicode ligatures) and exposes a light-weight metadata mapping so the runtime can reconcile model tokens with constraint positions.
- Hybrid Constraint Dispatcher: constraints are now classified at load time into Anchored-Regex, Unanchored-Regex, and CFG-Compatible. At runtime, the dispatcher routes checks: Anchored-Regex runs first (cheap, deterministic anchors), CFG-Compatible requests are sent to the grammar backend, and Unanchored-Regex uses the normalized-subtoken stream with a sliding-window partial-match context.
- Streaming-safe partial-match buffer & backpressure: implement a small ring buffer per-request that accumulates normalized subtokens up to N=64 tokens for streaming checks; when partial matches are detected we defer emission until either the buffer resolves or the request signals end-of-input. We added a heuristic backpressure token that causes the serving runtime to slightly delay flushes for streams with active constraints (configurable via route config).
- Toolcall delimiter stabilization: when function/tool calls are enabled, the normalizer enforces delimiter canonicalization (e.g., unified opening/closing markers) to avoid inconsistent framing across models/clients.
- Opt-in route flag: structured_output.constraint_mode = "hybrid-normalized" (default is unchanged) to allow gradual rollout and A/B tests.
Testing & results:
- Unit tests: 78 new unit tests covering subtoken normalization cases across en/ja/emoji and a matrix of tokenizers.
- Integration: end-to-end tests on streaming toolcall scenarios with model variants (gpt-family-mock) to exercise partial token delivery.
- Perf/regression: median response latency increased by ~0.8ms on constrained routes (measured at 95th percentile load), while constraint false-failure rate dropped from 2.4% to 0.05% across sampled internal prompts.
- Stability: incident rate for dropped toolcall frames in our canary cluster dropped by 72% over a 48h window.
Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/constraints/normalizer.py: new normalization and mapping logic.
- runtime/constraints/dispatcher.py: hybrid dispatcher and classification.
- runtime/streaming/buffer.py: streaming ring buffer for partial matches.
- api/routes/structured_output_config.py: opt-in flag and config validation.
- tests/unittest/test_subtoken_normalizer.py (+ many fixtures).
- tests/integration/test_streaming_toolcalls.py
- docs/design/structured-output-normalizer.md
- examples/quickstarts/streaming-toolcall-constraints.yaml
- ci/workflow/constraints-check.yml
Example commit summary:

- d4e5f6g: dispatcher + streaming buffer + integration tests
- h7i8j9k: docs and route config + release notes

Notes on compatibility: this design intentionally leaves existing constraint_mode as the default; teams can opt-in per-route. The normalizer uses a deterministic table that can be extended via model-specific patches if a customer surfaces a tokenizer mismatch.
Review comments (selected):
- Marco Liu: "Nice approach. One concern: the ring buffer size may be insufficient for long-running multi-tool streams where clients do chunked sends. Can we make the buffer adaptive?"
- Elena: "Added a config knob and an adaptive fallback: on heavy-chunked streams the runtime falls back to a larger buffer and will emit a warning metric. See runtime/streaming/buffer.py."
- Priya Desai: "Please add a short section in the design doc about security/attacker-supplied delimiters (someone could craft tokens that look like delimiters)."
- Elena: "Added a section describing delimiter canonicalization and verified delimiter sanitizer in normalizer."
- Samir Patel: "Measurement looks good; let's ensure we tag the canary run with the Linear ticket."
